title: Relative clauses: the products that each country exported

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* and *quien* from B1 Unit 5. A relative clause adds information to a noun and tells us which one we mean. History texts use it all the time: *the products that each country exported*, *the capital that paid for the railways*.

items.spanish: Los productos que exportaba cada país dependían de su tierra y de su clima.
items.english: The products that each country exported depended on its land and climate.

items.spanish: El capital que financió los ferrocarriles era sobre todo británico.
items.english: The capital that financed the railways was mostly British.

items.spanish: Los países que dependían de un solo producto quedaban expuestos.
items.english: The countries that depended on a single product were exposed.

items.spanish: Los comerciantes, que vendían los productos al exterior, ganaron mucho.
items.english: The merchants, who sold the products abroad, earned a lot.

sections.content: English can leave out "that" (*the products we sold*). Spanish never leaves out *que*: *los productos que vendíamos*. With commas, *que* adds extra information (*Los comerciantes, que vendían…*); without commas it tells us which ones.
